segments.text: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are going to talk about index fund investing and why it beats stock picking for most retail investors.
Studies show that over a 20-year period, more than 90 percent of actively managed funds underperform their benchmark index.
The S&P 500 has returned an average of 10 percent annually over the last 50 years, which is hard to beat consistently.
Warren Buffett himself has said that a low-cost index fund is the best investment most people can make over the long term.
Dollar-cost averaging into an index fund removes the emotional decision-making that causes most retail investors to buy high and sell low.
